title: Usage
$comment: Role: aggregated consumption for one call (docs/architecture.md §2; ocai/core/usage.py Usage) in omit-absent wire form. The dimensional model: each consumption pins one measured value to three OPEN string dimensions — what was consumed (modality), how it is counted (unit), and which bucket of the call it belongs to (source) — so a provider can report a dimension core has never named without a release (rule 6). Normalization rule (normative, per provider): the source buckets are DISJOINT — input excludes cached input, output excludes reasoning where the provider itemizes it — so a total is a plain sum and no token is ever counted twice; each dialect codec documents how it maps its wire fields onto the disjoint buckets. The currency unit is RESERVED for gateway-reported cost; first-party cost computation stays an interceptor's job, never the IR's.
description: What one call consumed: a list of measured consumptions, each pinned to open modality/unit/source dimensions over disjoint buckets.

consumptions.description: The measured consumptions for the call, in report order; omitted when the provider reported none.

consumption.$comment: ocai/core/usage.py Consumption — one measured quantity pinned to the dimensions that give it meaning. Not an IR envelope carrier: a plain value object like span.

value.description: The consumed amount. Numeric for counts; a string is legal for gateway-reported amounts (e.g. a decimal cost).

modality.description: The open code for what kind of content was consumed. Known canonical values: text, image, audio, video. Unknown values are legal and preserved verbatim.

unit.description: The open code for how the value is counted. Known canonical values: tokens, characters, requests, search_requests (measured billable searches), samples, currency (reserved for gateway-reported cost; the consumption's extensions carry the currency code). Unknown values are legal and preserved verbatim.

source.description: The open code for which DISJOINT bucket of the call this belongs to. Known canonical values: input (prompt, excluding cache reads), output (completion, excluding itemized reasoning), reasoning (itemized thinking), cached (cache-read input). Unknown values are legal and preserved verbatim.
